aboutItems.title: Our History
aboutItems.subtitle: From a Visionary Community Initiative to a Premier National TVET Centre of Excellence
aboutItems.description:
Loima Technical and Vocational College (LTVC) was established by the Government of Kenya through the Ministry of Education, State Department for Technical and Vocational Training, to address the pressing demand for high-grade technical and vocational skills in Turkana County and the wider Northern Kenyan region.

Founded as a flagship TVET institution under Kenya Vision 2030, the college broke ground with ultra-modern mechanical workshops, electrical laboratories, and ICT infrastructure. Since opening its gates, Loima TVC has transformed from an initial cohort into a thriving multi-disciplinary technical college offering fully accredited Artisan, Craft Certificate, and Diploma qualifications under TVET CDACC, KNEC, and NITA curricula.
mandates: Empower Northern Kenya youth with market-demanded hands-on competencies.
Bridge the industrial workforce gap through Competency-Based Education and Training (CBET).
Foster inclusive socio-economic development, self-employment, and entrepreneurship.
Maintain full statutory compliance with TVETA and the KNQF qualification framework.

aboutItems.title: Contact Us
aboutItems.subtitle: Direct Channels to Our Admissions Desk, Registrar, and Campus Headquarters
aboutItems.description:
We welcome prospective trainees, parents, guardians, and corporate partners to visit our main campus or reach out through our official direct channels. Our admissions team is on standby to assist with course selection, KUCCPS inter-institutional transfers, hostel bookings, and fee payment arrangements.

Our campus is conveniently situated approximately 1.5 km from Lorugum shopping centre, along the Lodwar–Uganda (Lodwar–Moroto) road, with reliable all-weather access, secure parking, and visitor reception facilities.
mandates: Prompt response to telephone and WhatsApp admissions enquiries (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm).
Guided campus and workshop walkthrough tours for visiting prospective students.
Immediate resolution of registry correspondence and student status verifications.
Direct coordination with high school career teachers for secondary outreach.

images.caption: Main administration gateway and visitor reception center.
Customer service desk welcoming parents and new applicants.

aboutItems.title: Office of Principal
aboutItems.subtitle: Chief Executive Leadership, Academic Vision, and Strategic Execution
aboutItems.description:
The Principal is the Chief Executive Officer and academic leader of Loima Technical and Vocational College, serving as the Secretary to the Board of Governors. The Principal is charged with the overall operational leadership, academic excellence, TVETA regulatory compliance, and fiscal management of the institution.

Working closely with the Ministry of Education and TVET CDACC, the Principal spearheads institutional modernization, curriculum delivery, and the establishment of sustainable industry linkages that guarantee high employment outcomes for our graduates.
mandates: Provide visionary executive leadership and maintain institutional academic excellence.
Ensure strict adherence to national TVET quality standards, KNQF guidelines, and TVETA licensing.
Oversee institutional budget execution, asset preservation, and human resource development.
Act as the chief public representative of the college to the Government, county authorities, and donors.

aboutItems.title: Office of Deputy Principal Administration
aboutItems.subtitle: Institutional Operations, Human Resources, Infrastructure, and Security
aboutItems.description:
The Office of the Deputy Principal (Administration) is the nerve center for campus operations, resource management, and institutional logistics. This office manages human resources, campus physical infrastructure, fleet logistics, procurement coordination, estate security, and non-teaching staff welfare.

Through proactive maintenance schedules and modern facility management, the office ensures an optimal, safe, and productive teaching and learning environment across the 35+ acre campus.
mandates: Coordinate institutional staff recruitment, capacity development, and performance appraisal.
Supervise campus physical development, building maintenance, water, and power installations.
Ensure 24/7 security of trainees, staff, and institutional assets across campus grounds.
Manage transport fleet, workshop consumable supplies, and environmental cleanliness.
aboutItems.contactInfo: Email: dpa@loimatvc.ac.ke | Location: Administration Block, 1st Floor

aboutItems.title: Office of Deputy Principal Academics
aboutItems.subtitle: Curriculum Implementation, Examination Integrity, and Faculty Development
aboutItems.description:
The Office of the Deputy Principal (Academics) steers the educational core of the college. This office is tasked with curriculum implementation, timetable coordination, faculty supervision, academic quality audits, and statutory collaboration with examination bodies including TVET CDACC, KNEC, and NITA.

Under its stewardship, Loima TVC maintains a rigorous Competency-Based Education and Training (CBET) framework that combines 70% practical workshop immersion with 30% theory, ensuring trainees achieve complete occupational competence.
mandates: Plan, monitor, and evaluate the delivery of all approved TVET training programs.
Coordinate continuous assessments, internal moderation, and national examination schedules.
Ensure faculty members are certified in CBET methodologies and industry pedagogy.
Supervise academic departments and drive trainee academic performance.

aboutItems.title: ICT and Business Studies
aboutItems.subtitle: Computing Systems, Software Development, Accounting, and Enterprise Management
aboutItems.description:
The Department of ICT and Business Studies bridges technological mastery with enterprise management. Our state-of-the-art computer laboratories are equipped with high-speed fiber internet, server racks, and licensed development software to prepare trainees for the digital economy.

The department offers courses in Information Communication Technology, Business Management, Accounting, Human Resource Management, and Computerized Secretarial Studies, equipping graduates to launch tech enterprises or manage corporate operations.
mandates: Equip trainees with industry-standard software programming, database, and network skills.
Train professional accountants, procurement specialists, and enterprise managers.
Integrate artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and digital literacy across all training.
Facilitate incubation of tech startups and student digital innovations.

images.caption: Trainees working in the Ultra-Modern Computer Laboratory.
Business and accounting trainees conducting financial simulations.

aboutItems.title: Hospitality and Institutional Management
aboutItems.subtitle: Culinary Arts, Food & Beverage Production, Housekeeping, and Event Management
aboutItems.description:
The Department of Hospitality and Institutional Management prepares trainees for dynamic careers in the global tourism, hotel, and institutional catering sectors. Training is conducted in standard commercial training kitchens, mock hotel guest suites, and pastry bakeries.

Students gain hands-on expertise in international gastronomy, food safety and hygiene (HACCP), front office operations, mixology, housekeeping, and large-scale catering management.
mandates: Master professional culinary arts, baking, and international cuisine preparation.
Deliver world-class service training in restaurant, banqueting, and front office operations.
Instill rigorous food safety, nutrition, and institutional management standards.
Partner with top safari lodges, hotels, and airlines for trainee attachments.

images.caption: Hospitality trainees during practical culinary baking session.
Food and beverage service practicals in the training restaurant.

aboutItems.title: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
aboutItems.subtitle: Power Systems, Industrial Automation, Solar PV Technology, and Building Wiring
aboutItems.description:
The Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering produces skilled electrical technologists and technicians. Featuring dedicated power distribution trainers, AC/DC motor benches, and solar PV demonstration rigs, the department provides comprehensive training.

Trainees are prepared for direct EPRA (Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority) electrical worker licensing, enabling them to execute domestic and industrial installations, transformer maintenance, and renewable energy projects.
mandates: Provide comprehensive practical training in domestic, commercial, and industrial electrical wiring.
Train solar photovoltaic installers aligned with national clean energy targets.
Prepare trainees for EPRA Class C, B, and A statutory licensing examinations.
Master electric motor maintenance, rewinding, switchgear, and PLC automation.

images.caption: Trainees assembling industrial power distribution boards.
Electrical workshop testing bench and oscilloscope analysis.

aboutItems.title: Department of Agriculture and Applied Sciences
aboutItems.subtitle: Climate-Smart Farming, Agribusiness Value Addition, Animal Health, and Irrigation
aboutItems.description:
Positioned in the agricultural heartbeat of Turkana County, the Department of Agriculture and Applied Sciences champions modern, climate-smart agriculture and sustainable food systems. The department manages a dedicated demonstration farm, modern greenhouses, and drip irrigation installations.

Students receive rigorous training in crop production, livestock husbandry, post-harvest handling, agribusiness management, veterinary technology, and soil nutrient analysis.
mandates: Teach modern drip irrigation and climate-resilient crop farming methods.
Equip trainees with livestock breeding, dairy management, and veterinary skills.
Train agribusiness entrepreneurs in product processing and market value addition.
Provide extension services and agricultural advisory to local farming communities.

images.caption: Agricultural trainees inspecting high-yield crops under greenhouse cultivation.
Field demonstration of computerized drip irrigation and soil testing.

aboutItems.title: Building & Civil Engineering
aboutItems.subtitle: Structural Masonry, Plumbing, Architectural Draughting, and Surveying
aboutItems.description:
The Department of Building & Civil Engineering equips trainees to build Kenya’s critical infrastructure. With outdoor construction yards, surveying gear, and plumbing test installations, trainees gain practical mastery in masonry, architectural design, pipefitting, concrete technology, and road construction.

Graduates gain accreditation through the National Construction Authority (NCA) and secure employment with major construction firms, county governments, and water companies.
mandates: Develop skilled craftsmen in structural masonry, bricklaying, and plastering.
Provide practical mastery of residential and municipal plumbing, drainage, and solar water heating.
Train architectural draughting using modern CAD software and computerized surveying levels.
Foster independent construction contractors accredited under the NCA framework.

images.caption: Building technology trainees constructing brickwork and structural foundations.
Plumbing and pipefitting trainees testing pressurized hydraulic lines.

aboutItems.title: Sports and Recreation Office
aboutItems.subtitle: Physical Fitness, Inter-TVET Athletics, Co-Curricular Excellence, and Wellness
aboutItems.description:
The Sports and Recreation Office coordinates physical health, sporting championships, and recreational life at Loima TVC. The college maintains football pitches, volleyball courts, netball courts, and indoor games facilities.

Our teams participate actively in the Kenya Association of Technical Training Institutions (KATTI) regional and national athletics, ball games, and cultural competitions, winning laurels and fostering teamwork and discipline among trainees.
mandates: Organize competitive sports teams in football, volleyball, athletics, and basketball.
Coordinate participation in KATTI regional and national TVET sports championships.
Promote daily fitness, wellness, and recreational activities for all trainees and staff.
Provide leadership and talent scouting opportunities for gifted student athletes.

images.caption: Loima TVC trainees competing in regional TVET track and field events.
Campus football and team fitness training sessions.

aboutItems.title: Industrial Liaison Office
aboutItems.subtitle: Mandatory Industrial Attachments, Corporate Partnerships, and Workplace Placements
aboutItems.description:
The Industrial Liaison Office (ILO) bridges the classroom with actual industry. It coordinates mandatory 3-month industrial attachments for all trainees prior to graduation, securing placements across leading manufacturing firms, engineering agencies, agribusiness conglomerates, and government parastatals.

The office also manages trainee workplace insurance (WIBA), organizes on-site supervisor assessments, and builds long-term memoranda of understanding (MOUs) with national employers.
mandates: Facilitate 100% industrial attachment placement for all eligible Craft and Diploma trainees.
Administer statutory group personal accident and WIBA workplace insurance coverage.
Coordinate faculty supervision visits and employer attachment assessment rubrics.
Formulate industry MoUs for apprenticeship, dual training, and graduate hiring.

images.caption: Trainees undergoing industrial apprenticeship at an engineering partner plant.
Industrial liaison officer signing an MOU with corporate partners.

aboutItems.title: Office of Career Services
aboutItems.subtitle: Employability Training, Resume Clinics, Mock Interviews, and Job Placement
aboutItems.description:
The Office of Career Services (OCS) empowers trainees to transition seamlessly from graduation to rewarding careers. Established under Ministry of Education guidelines, the OCS hosts regular career days, resume-writing workshops, soft skills bootcamps, and mock interview sessions.

The office maintains an active employer database and graduate tracking network, connecting Loima TVC alumni directly to job opportunities in the private sector and public civil service.
mandates: Conduct regular professional CV writing, digital branding, and interview preparation clinics.
Organize the annual Loima TVC Career & Innovation Fair with invited corporate recruiters.
Track alumni employment destinations and maintain graduate employer feedback loops.
Deliver entrepreneurial mentorship for trainees seeking to establish independent businesses.

images.caption: Career advisor conducting a one-on-one interview preparation session.
Students attending the annual Loima TVC corporate recruitment forum.

aboutItems.title: Quality Assurance & Standards Office
aboutItems.subtitle: Institutional Audits, TVETA Compliance, CBET Benchmarking, and Evaluation
aboutItems.description:
The Quality Assurance and Standards (QAS) Office safeguards the educational and operational excellence of the college. Acting as an internal watchdog, the office carries out regular internal quality audits of training facilities, lecturer lesson plans, practical assessment scoring, and student satisfaction.

The office ensures Loima TVC continually complies with TVETA licensing conditions, ISO standards, and the Kenya National Qualifications Framework (KNQF) requirements.
mandates: Conduct continuous internal academic and administrative audits across all departments.
Monitor curriculum delivery to ensure 100% adherence to TVET CDACC CBET standards.
Administer confidential end-of-term trainee feedback and lecturer evaluation surveys.
Lead institutional preparations for external TVETA and statutory regulatory inspections.

images.caption: Quality Assurance team conducting an academic standards review.
Inspection of workshop safety protocols and practical rubrics.

aboutItems.title: Finance Office
aboutItems.subtitle: Fee Administration, Government Capitation, HELB Disbursements, and Budgeting
aboutItems.description:
The Finance Office manages the financial integrity, accounting, and revenue systems of Loima TVC. Responsible for trainee fee billing, the office ensures transparent management of the annual Government Capitation subsidy per student, HELB TVET loan and bursary disbursements, and NG-CDF tuition sponsorships.

Trainees and parents receive timely financial receipts, fee payment installment reconciliations, and clearance statements via secure institutional accounts.
mandates: Process trainee tuition fees, capitation remittances, and HELB loan statements.
Provide instant receipts and digitized clearance statements for registered students.
Ensure strict adherence to the Public Finance Management (PFM) Act and statutory audits.
Liaise with national banks (KCB) and M-Pesa paybill channels for secure fee remittance.

images.caption: Finance team balancing tuition ledgers and trainee bursary accounts.
Accounts desk issuing official receipts and fee statements.

aboutItems.contactInfo: Accounts Desk: finance@loimatvc.ac.ke | Location: Admin Block Ground Floor

aboutItems.title: Performance Contracting Office
aboutItems.subtitle: Institutional Target Setting, Public Service Evaluation, and Compliance Reporting
aboutItems.description:
The Performance Contracting Office steers the college’s compliance with the Government of Kenya Performance Contracting guidelines for State Corporations and Tertiary Institutions.

The office cascades annual ministerial targets to all academic and non-academic departments, monitors quarterly milestone delivery, and prepares statutory performance reports submitted to the Ministry of Education and the Public Service Commission.
mandates: Negotiate and execute the annual Performance Contract with the Ministry of Education.
Cascade performance deliverables to departments and individual staff workplans.
Conduct quarterly internal performance evaluations and statutory compliance reviews.
Spearhead continual institutional productivity and public service delivery enhancements.

images.caption: Performance contracting committee deliberating on quarterly targets.
Institutional performance reporting and documentation review.

aboutItems.title: Examinations & Timetabling Office
aboutItems.subtitle: National Examination Administration, KNEC/CDACC Registrations, and Schedules
aboutItems.description:
The Examinations and Timetabling Office is responsible for the scheduling, organization, and administration of all internal and national examinations. The office oversees candidate registration with KNEC, TVET CDACC, and NITA, manages examination secure storage, and supervises assessment rooms.

Additionally, the office drafts the master teaching and workshop usage timetables each term, ensuring balanced facility utilization across all faculties without scheduling clashes.
mandates: Register all eligible trainees for national KNEC, TVET CDACC, and NITA examinations.
Manage secure handling, printing, and confidential administration of examination papers.
Formulate termly master class and workshop practical timetables.
Facilitate timely release of internal progress records and official national examination results.

images.caption: Trainees sitting for national certification examinations.
Examination office processing official candidate registration dockets.

aboutItems.title: Research & Innovation Office
aboutItems.subtitle: Applied Engineering Research, Prototype Incubation, Robotics, and Patenting
aboutItems.description:
The Research and Innovation Office fosters a culture of discovery, technological ingenuity, and problem-solving at Loima TVC. Trainees and trainers are supported to build practical prototypes that solve local challenges—such as solar water pumps, automated agro-sorters, waste-plastic pavers, and mobile IoT applications.

The office sponsors trainee participation in regional TVET innovation fairs, scientific conferences, and technology incubation competitions with industry mentors.
mandates: Promote applied research and engineering prototyping among trainees and faculty.
Organize the annual Loima TVC Trainee Innovation and Science Competition.
Facilitate patenting and intellectual property (IP) protection for breakthrough inventions.
Secure research grants and technical equipment sponsorships from technology partners.

images.caption: Engineering trainees testing an automated robotic prototyping rig.
Student researchers demonstrating solar-powered agricultural prototypes.
